method_config.candidate_source: WordNet first sense; base-form NN/JJ/RB/VB; lowercase lexical core in one GPT2 token in the exact rendered context; verified original causal prefix
method_config.description: Fixed seed codebook; two selectors; external payload length costs 32 bits; full serialized codebook counted separately; no semantic guarantee

token_alignment.rendering: Original cover prefix + candidate + original suffix, preserving actual whitespace and punctuation.
token_alignment.candidate_span: The full lowercase alphabetic core must occupy exactly one token ending at the core end; no suffix absorption.
token_alignment.causal_prefix: Candidate token index and every preceding token ID must match the original cover tokenization before reusing original-cover logits.
token_alignment.first_token: Reject the first token because this protocol supplies no BOS conditioning token.
token_alignment.rejection: Reject unaligned or multi-token candidates before constructing payload-independent groups; count considered/admitted/rejected candidate pairs.

explanation.template: A reader has asked what matters when {topic}. Write an English explanation of approximately 180 words that connects the main ideas in ordinary prose. Give no title, dialogue, bullet points, or numbered list.

instructions.template: Describe a sensible beginning, middle, and end for {topic}. Write approximately 180 English words as connected paragraphs, explaining why actions are ordered that way. Omit headings and list formatting.

narrative.template: Follow one ordinary person through a small event involving {topic}. Tell the event in approximately 180 English words, with a clear beginning and ending and no title or dialogue.

explanation.template: Draft a short explanatory memo for a community group about {topic}. In approximately 180 English words, connect the purpose, main ideas, and likely consequences. Use prose paragraphs without a title, salutation, or list.

instructions.template: Write a handover note for a colleague who will take responsibility for {topic}. Explain the preparation and practical sequence in approximately 180 English words of connected prose, without headings, bullet points, or numbering.

narrative.template: Write a fictional incident account describing a small complication during {topic} and its resolution. Use a neutral observer viewpoint and approximately 180 English words of narrative prose, without headings, lists, or dialogue.

explanation.template: Write the body of a friendly letter explaining {topic} to someone curious about it. Develop the ideas and reasons in approximately 180 English words of flowing prose. Omit addresses, greetings, signatures, headings, and lists.

instructions.template: Write the body of a letter advising a friend who is about to try {topic}. Give the preparation, main actions, and reasons in approximately 180 English words of natural prose, with no greeting, signature, title, bullet points, or numbered steps.

narrative.template: Write a fictional personal journal entry recalling an ordinary episode involving {topic}. Describe what happened and bring the episode to a definite close in approximately 180 English words of narrative prose. Omit a date line, title, lists, and dialogue.

duplicate_policy.normalization: Unicode word tokens, casefold, whitespace join

pilot_limitations: Four test topic clusters cannot establish broad generalization.
External length framing requires accounting for 32 bits outside stegotext.
No superiority or security claim follows from a feasibility pilot.
Human semantic and grammatical evaluation is not part of this automated pilot.
v1 completed but its raw artifacts were lost; v3 does not replace or pool those observations.
v2 stayed at the initial remote-checkpoint gate with zero generation attempts in the last verified state; no initial receipt was issued. Its unused topics and prompts are reused openly.
All nine prompt templates request approximately 180 words; a common 384-token ceiling may still truncate outputs.
Prompt templates and topic families are disjoint by design; unique IDs do not by themselves prove semantic independence.
The corrected quality selector uses a local original-cover-context next-token proxy, not actual stegotext perplexity or a semantic-quality guarantee.
Verified prefix alignment fixes the artificial leading-space error; interactions between multiple substitutions remain unmodeled and rejected alignments can reduce capacity.

run_identity.reason: Fresh frozen run after transient environment reset, with a pre-generation correction to rendered candidate tokenization and new seeds.
run_identity.prior_v1_status: Observed completed by executing agent; raw artifacts lost and observations not independently verifiable.
run_identity.prior_v2_status: Zero generation attempts in the last verified state; initial remote receipt never issued; local freeze artifacts lost in the subsequent environment reset.
run_identity.method_change_from_v2: Exact rendered candidate tokenization, verified original causal prefix, and explicit rejection of unaligned candidates replace the artificial leading-space tokenization.
run_identity.reuse_of_v2_design: All ten unused topic texts/IDs and nine unused prompt templates/family IDs are intentionally identical to v2. No v2 generated text or outcome was observed.

prompt_design.train_form: General reader explanation, procedural account, and third-person story.
prompt_design.development_form: Explanatory memo, handover note, and neutral incident account.
prompt_design.test_form: Explanatory letter, advice letter, and personal journal entry.
prompt_design.guarantee: Distinct exact templates and declared communicative families; no claim of absolute semantic independence.
prompt_design.origin: Unexecuted v2 design; original v2 identifiers retained to make reuse explicit.
